indexPrompt.moe-balance-loss-lower-bound: A two-expert layer routes each token to the expert with the higher router probability and adds the lesson's auxiliary loss, alpha times N times the sum over experts of f_i times P_i. Find the loss of one uneven batch, prove the lowest value the loss can take over every possible batch, and compute the gradient that training actually follows.
indexPrompt.moe-balance-loss-top-two: A layer with four experts routes each token to its two most probable experts. Given the router probabilities for a batch of four tokens, compute the auxiliary load-balancing loss as a multiple of alpha.
indexPrompt.moe-bias-after-update: A layer with four experts sends each token to its top two and balances its load with the bias rule from the lesson, stepping each bias by 0.05. After a step in which experts 1 and 2 were overloaded and experts 3 and 4 underloaded, the biases are (-0.15, -0.05, 0.10, 0.20), and the next token arrives with scores (0.85, 0.70, 0.65, 0.60). Which two experts does it go to, and what gate weight does each of them get?
indexPrompt.moe-bias-settles: A layer with two experts routes each token to the larger biased score and nudges the two routing biases to even out the load, with the score differences spread uniformly. Find how many updates it takes for the experts to receive equal shares, how many tokens then go to the expert they scored lower on, and what happens when every token has the same score difference.
indexPrompt.moe-capacity-drops: A layer with four experts sends each token to its top two, and one batch of 1,000 tokens gives the assignment counts per expert. Work out how many assignments a capacity limit drops, the largest number of tokens that could skip the layer entirely, and the padding left by the smallest limit that drops nothing.
indexPrompt.moe-splitting-experts: A Switch-style layer with 16 experts is split into 64 smaller ones that hold the same parameters and cost the same FLOPs per token. Work out how many different sets of four experts a token can be sent to, how many bytes of all-to-all traffic one token causes after the split, and how much of that traffic is saved when a device that holds two or more of the token's experts gets the vector only once.
indexPrompt.moe-switch-gate-gradient: A Switch-style layer sends each token to the one expert with the highest router probability and scales that expert's output by that probability. Given the four router probabilities, the chosen expert's output and the gradient reaching the layer's output, what is the gradient for the four router logits?
indexPrompt.moe-top-two-router-gradient: A Mixtral-style layer sends each token to its two most probable experts and renormalizes their weights. Given the router probabilities, the two chosen experts' outputs and the gradient reaching the layer's output, find the gradient with respect to every router logit, and say what the router learns at the first step when every expert is an identical copy of one trained network.
